public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no decisive event was established. Google documents a world-model prototype, while ARC Prize observes a GPT-family model constructing symbolic world models during a benchmark. Neither finding proves that a new core architecture is necessary, or supplies a validated trustworthy general AI counterexample.
limitations: Behavior on a bounded benchmark cannot establish broad trustworthiness.
Public descriptions may not disclose enough architecture to distinguish built-in mechanisms from generated representations.
One successful implementation would show feasibility more readily than necessity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Trustworthy AI will require genuinely new architectures with explicit knowledge and world models at their core.

statement.excerpt: For that, we will, I predict, need genuinely new architectures that incorporate explicit knowledge and world models at their very core.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-5

our_interpretation: For that refers in context to broadly capable AI that people can trust, rather than a reliable system for one narrow task.
Need asserts necessity. Showing that one successful system uses world models would not alone prove they are required.
At their very core means central architectural mechanisms, not merely optional external tools or temporary representations generated during a task.
Genuinely new is read relative to the GPT-style architectures discussed in the post.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evidence establishes that achieving broadly trustworthy general AI requires a materially new architecture centered on explicit knowledge and world models, with convincing evidence that these features are necessary rather than merely useful.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independently validated, broadly trustworthy general AI system achieves the relevant capabilities without a materially new architecture centered on explicit knowledge and world models.
